intro: An online comparison can combine two ranked lists into one display. Alternating ownership while skipping duplicate documents keeps credit assignment explicit.
task: Combine two rankings into a deduplicated display while recording which ranking supplied each document.
requirements: left and right are vectors of integer-valued document IDs in [0,1000000], possibly empty and with repetitions. k is an integer 0..1000000.
Starting with left, alternate turns. On each turn take that ranking’s next unseen ID; if exhausted, take the other ranking’s next unseen ID. Stop after k unique documents or exhaustion of both.
Return dict documents as selected IDs and owners as 0 for a left pick or 1 for a right pick. Advance the scheduled turn after each successful selection, even when the other ranking supplied it.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Track displayed IDs globally
hints.body: A document selected from either ranking must be skipped in both future scans.

hints.title: Separate scheduled turn from actual owner
hints.body: An exhausted ranking can borrow a pick, but the recorded owner is the ranking that supplied it.

explanation: Interleaving produces a shared display with a record of which ranking supplied each result. Removing duplicates prevents one document from occupying several display positions.

This deterministic alternating variant always starts left; it is not randomized, count-balanced team-draft interleaving. A real randomized comparison must address starting-order effects, click attribution, and experimental validity separately.
